title: 2026 Preseason
coldOpen: Six playoff spots. Twelve owners. Roughly ten legitimate plans to get there and two guys who are at least being honest with themselves. Welcome to the return of the PDL Power Rankings, preseason edition.

1: Well, this is embarrassing.
We created the power rankings.
We asked everyone to rank the teams. we recorded a podcast about the rankings. I am now spending an irresponsible amount of my free time writing about the rankings.
And one of you ranked my team 10th.
Tenth.
I basically invented Yelp and then found out somebody left my restaurant one star.

For six straight years the Delco Dreamers have made the playoffs. Longest streak in league history. There was a time when this team was actually feared, which younger readers may have trouble believing because most of the evidence has been destroyed.
Now we're sixth.
One guy thinks we're tenth.

Darren has been telling me this team is old and dying for about four years, and every year I’ve gotten to point at another playoff appearance and tell him to fuck off. It became one of my favorite traditions.
Unfortunately, I think the bastard may have just been early.

I finally started moving some of the old guys. Davante is gone. Derrick Henry is gone. A few years ago this roster had enough aging superstars that every Sunday looked like an NFL Films documentary narrated by someone discussing the passage of time. But they scored points. I didn't care.
Now some of them are gone, and I have discovered why I kept them.
They were good.
What’s left is basically Lamar Jackson and Jalen Hurts holding the Dreamers above sea level while I stand behind them insisting everything is fine.

Jalen Hurts even spent this week going viral because the Eagles released helmet-cam footage that allowed the entire internet to experience one of his interceptions over the middle from his own point of view.
Really cool technology.
Love finally being able to see my problems firsthand.

Lamar is still Lamar, thankfully, and Tyler Shough gives me a young QB3 that I’m probably already way too emotionally invested in because I desperately need proof that there is life after the current roster dies.
The receivers are where I start lying to myself.
DeVonta Smith.
Marvin Harrison Jr.
DK Metcalf.
That’s good!
Look at that!
See?
We're fine.

Marvin Harrison has spent part of August generating clips for dropping footballs at Cardinals camp, which is exactly what I needed while trying to write a section about how the Dreamers still have young cornerstone talent.
Appreciate you, Mitsubishi Marv.
Then I saw where the cibe my roster was and thought, you know what? Let's add Aiyuk to this.
At this point Brandon Aiyuk isn’t a dynasty asset.
Tyler Warren is at least young. DeVonta is still young enough. Marvin is young. Shough is...well, no, he's not young.
I have begun listing players’ ages to calm myself down.
That's where we are.
The real problem is running back.
Darren’s assessment is not only concise, but is accurate:
“Your running backs suck.”
Thank you Darren.
I don't need to win the league.
Obviously I would like to.
But there is now something much more important at stake.
I need to find out who ranked me tenth and make that person watch this corpse of a team play in Week 15.
That’s enough motivation for me.
#6 Delco Dreamers.
Still in the playoff picture according to the preseason rankings, assholes.
For now.
2: Joe inherited Steve's dynasty team, and it is one of those that looks a lot better when you’re just reading the names.
Mahomes. Saquon. A.J. Brown. Burden.
You see those names and think alright, there’s something here.
Then you remember this team missed the playoffs last year.

So I’m not going to act as if Joe walked into a golden situation, but compared to the other vacant team this year, he kind of did. The Crocs were fine. Probably could’ve made another run at it with a few moves, maybe snuck into the playoffs, maybe spent three months telling us they were “dangerous if they got in” before losing by 34 in the first round. We’ve all owned that team.
Joe wanted nothing to do with it.
He started selling.
And kept selling.

Anything on the roster with a recognizable name and current value eventually found its way onto Facebook Marketplace. By the end of the offseason, Connecticut had gone from borderline playoff team to completely unrecognizable.
But what he was able to acquire from all those superstars is something to behold:
Nine 2027 first-round picks (and it looks like he has 1.01 and 1.02 locked up).
I keep typing that out because it still looks fake.
Nine. [JJ McCarthy.jpg]

Joe now controls 75% of the first round of a draft that dynasty people have already spent two years jerking off to, and we’re still a full season away from the hype getting genuinely unbearable. Jeremiah Smith could catch a slant against Akron this fall and by October somebody in this league will value a 2027 first like beachfront property.
Joe has nine of them.
Joe saw the team that Steve has been assembling for years and was like "Nah."

Now whether nine firsts becomes the foundation of a monster or we’re all laughing about this three years from now while Connecticut is starting Jeremiah Smith, seven WR3s and a running back who currently attends prom, I have no idea.
Joe might know.
It would be nice if he talked to us.

That has become an interesting part of the Connecticut Crocs experience. Brian brings his friend Joe into the league, Joe shows up, executes about 40% of the league’s offseason trade volume, acquires nine first-round picks and then essentially stops communicating.
I’m supposed to believe this is a real guy? Apparently he is the brains behind LF and writes everything...so it looks like I have found a longform writing rival as well?
I have no evidence that Joe isn’t just Brian on an incognito tab.
Until Joe gets irrationally angry about a Thursday night holding call or sends a trade offer at 6:14 in the morning while taking a dump, I’m keeping an open mind.
We currently have more public evidence surrounding Mike Vrabel and Dianna Russini than we do of signs of life with "Joe."

And Brian picked a pretty smart burner account strategy too. You can’t have the fake owner immediately trade all the good players to Hollywood Hu$tle. Too obvious. No, you spend a year accumulating nine firsts first. Play the long game.
I’m watching you, Brian.
As for Connecticut, there really isn’t much football analysis to do right now. The roster is supposed to suck.

Joe traded away the present for an absolutely stupid amount of control over 2027, and now he gets to spend this season doing what every committed dynasty rebuilder eventually discovers is the purest form of fantasy football:
rooting against other people’s teams because you own their picks.
Welcome to the league.
3: I don’t know what happened to Jeff this offseason.

For years, this was one of the most patient people in the league. He ate shit. He accumulated picks. He rebuilt. He sat at the bottom while the rest of us actually played fantasy football and kept telling himself that someday all of this would be worth it.
Then one day, Jeff said enough.
Patrick Mahomes.
Joe Burrow.
Saquon Barkley.
Christian McCaffrey.
James Cook.
Kenneth Walker.
A.J. Brown.
Davante Adams.

And those are just some of the names that moved through Wichita during an offseason where opening the league transaction feed started to feel like checking Woj during NBA free agency (sorry for the basketball reference, Greggy).
Jeff was everywhere.
Firsts. Seconds. Thirds. Future firsts. Players. More picks. Whatever.
At one point, I’m pretty sure the only thing stopping Jeff from trading more picks was that Sleeper didn't have the option yet.
The Rams spent this offseason trading premium draft capital for Trent McDuffie and then Myles Garrett, continuing the most aggressive “fuck them picks” operation in actual professional football.
Jeff saw Les Snead do that and apparently thought:
Pussy.
Because this is probably the most violent transition from rebuild to contention we’ve ever had in the PDL.
There was no gradual ramp-up. No “let’s see how the young guys develop and maybe buy at the deadline.”
Jeff went from collecting assets to kicking the door open with Mahomes and Burrow.
There were seasons where Wichita being near the bottom was not uncommon. We didn't have to discuss it. Jeff himself openly accepted that he was building toward something years away.
Now somebody ranked him first in the entire league.
It’s also hard to argue with when you actually look at the lineup.
The running backs alone are stupid.
McCaffrey. Saquon. James Cook. Kenneth Walker.
The podcast realization that Saquon and Walker are flex players on this team was when it really registered for me how ridiculous the spending spree had gotten.
There are teams in this league that would kill to have those two as their RB1 and RB2.
Jeff is moving them around depending on what he feels like that week.

The funny part is that CMC is currently missing camp with “tightness,” which has already inspired an entire conspiracy theory that he’s secretly holding in for more money. Ian Rapoport says the tightness is legitimate and he’s expected to be ready for Week 1.
That feels like the only appropriate way for Jeff’s first true all-in season to begin.
Spend some time rebuilding.
Cash everything in.
Christian McCaffrey: tightness.
Welcome back to competitive fantasy football.

There are holes. The receiver depth drops faster than the ridiculous collection of names at quarterback and running back. Tight end isn’t giving him the same advantage other contenders have. If the old guys start acting old at the same time, this could get uncomfortable quickly.
But I also think we need to stop grading Wichita like it’s still a rebuild.
Jeff isn’t trying to win KeepTradeCut anymore.
Jeff actually cashed the chips in.
He has Patrick Mahomes and Joe Burrow at quarterback.
He has a running back room that looks like somebody turned trade override on in Madden.
And after years of watching Wichita patiently collect scraps at the bottom of the standings, Jeff finally decided he’d like to ruin everyone else's Sunday for a while.
I may be one of Wichita's biggest fans this season.
4: This one looks wrong.
Murphy Street Empire at #8.

I went back to it a few times because MSE has basically lived in the upper class of this league since we started doing this shit. There are certain teams you get used to seeing near the top, and Max has been one of them. Tier 1. Every year. Maybe the roster changes, maybe one season goes sideways, whatever. You still assume Murphy Street is going to be involved.
And now they're one tier away from the bottom of the barrel.
Disgusting.
I don’t even think MSE is bad.

Ja’Marr Chase is still Ja’Marr Chase. Ladd McConkey. Chase Brown. Kyle Pitts. Dak. There are actual stars here, and then Max added the Cam Ward/Carnell Tate stack because Brett apparently decided Max had suffered enough.

That stack could end up being a massive deal for this team. Tennessee drafted Tate fourth overall specifically while trying to build around Ward, and Ward has already been talking about what Tate can add to the offense. If Ward makes the Year 2 jump people are expecting, Max suddenly has the kind of young QB/WR combination that can drag the entire age curve of this roster back in the right direction.
Which Max desperately needed after C.J. Stroud decided to ruin everything.
I don’t know what the hell happened there. I know everyone is expecting a bounce-back with him, but really, wtf happened?

There was a point where having Stroud and Nico together felt unfair. Stroud comes into the league, immediately looks like one of the next great quarterbacks, Max has Nico attached to him, and of course MSE has stumbled into another foundational stack that we’re all going to have to deal with for the next seven years.
Then Stroud just... stopped being that guy.

He’d still give you enough to remember the rookie season and then spend stretches looking like somebody had swapped him with Nathan Peterman. Even now Houston is entering 2026 with people asking whether Stroud can get back to that original trajectory. That question has hung around long enough that Max finally stopped waiting for the answer.
Nico got cashed in.
The Stroud/Nico stack is dead.
Ward/Tate is the new religion.

I actually like that move for Max because this roster needed something new to grow around. You can only stare lovingly at Ja’Marr Chase for so many years before eventually realizing there are other roster spots.
Because the first handful of names still looks like Murphy Street.
Then you keep scrolling.
Coker.
Doubs.
Oh.

They’re fine. Nobody is opening Sleeper on Sunday morning terrified because Jalen Coker is sitting in Max’s flex. Romeo Doubs isn’t some roster embarrassment either, I’d take him on my team. It’s just that this season the PDL has gotten ridiculous. Teams that used to have a couple soft spots now have legitimate starters sitting there. The margin disappeared.
That’s probably the real explanation for #8.

A few years ago this version of Murphy Street might still comfortably sit in the upper half of the league because Chase can win weeks by himself, Dak gives you points, Pitts is useful, Ladd is excellent, Chase Brown is there, and you talk yourself into the rest.
Now I look at some of the teams above Max, and the flex difference is where this starts to tell the story.
Which is insane considering where MSE has historically lived.

Maybe this ranking ages horribly. It absolutely could. Carnell Tate hits immediately. Ward takes off. Pitts finally becomes the player fantasy football has been promising us since the Obama administration. Ladd keeps doing Ladd things. Ja’Marr goes nuclear because that's just a thing he occasionally does to ruin somebody's Sunday.
Suddenly Max is 6-2 and I’m trying to quietly delete this.
Wouldn’t be the first time MSE made us look stupid.
There’s also another possibility that feels strange to even write.
Maybe the window actually closed.

Not slammed shut; everybody gets traded, blow the whole thing up. I don’t mean that. But don't be surprised if some moves are made if it doesn't go according to plan. Max is probably a few steps ahead of us.
MSE used to be one of the teams everyone else was measuring against.
Now I’m measuring MSE against everybody else.
And I’m not sure Max is going to enjoy it.
#8 Murphy Street Empire
Jesus.
5: Joe got Mahomes, Saquon and A.J. Brown to liquidate.
Jon got Michael’s team.
Little different.

Darren brought Jon in from work to take over the other vacant franchise this offseason, and I really don’t know how much warning he gave him beforehand. Michael had been all over the place with this roster. Buying, selling, rebuilding, maybe contending, actually never mind we’re rebuilding again. There were times where I’m not convinced Michael knew what direction the team was going until Sleeper sent the trade notification.
So Jon tearing it apart made sense.
I would’ve torn it apart too.

The problem was there wasn’t a Mahomes sitting around to turn into a mountain of future firsts. Jon was working with what Michael left him, and if he wanted to get younger quickly he was going to have to take some swings.
He took a lot of them on this rookie class.
A rookie class, by the way, that dynasty people spent the previous year treating like the vegetables at a cookout.
Jon bought anyway.
Makai Lemon. Jordyn Tyson. Omar Cooper. Kenyon Sadiq. Fernando Mendoza. Ty Simpson. He pushed a lot of his rebuild into this group.
August has been fucking brutal for the Crocs.
Lemon has spent most of the offseason fighting a hamstring injury.
Tyson is now expected to miss about two months with his own hamstring injury.

Omar Cooper was a first-round NFL draft pick and opened the preseason looking up at Isaiah Williams on the Jets depth chart. Isaiah Williams. I had to make sure I had the right Isaiah Williams before I wrote this.
Sadiq had hernia surgery and has spent the summer working his way back from that.
Darren has to see Jon at work.
I keep coming back to that.

Imagine talking your coworker into joining the dynasty league you’ve been in for years, handing him Michael’s roster, and four months later he’s spending his lunch break reading about Jordyn Tyson’s hamstring.
What do you even say the one time a month Jon decides to stroll into the office?
Tom Brady spent this week complaining that NFL players are looking for ways out of preseason. Send him Jon’s number. Jon has several guys who would probably love to participate in one.
And yes, I know.
It’s August.
I can already hear it.

Lemon’s career isn’t over because he pulled a hamstring. Tyson missing the beginning of his rookie season doesn’t suddenly make him a bust. Cooper could be starting for the Jets two months from now and nobody will remember who was ahead of him on a preseason depth chart. Sadiq is already working his way back.
All true.
I would still be shitting myself.

Because Jon doesn’t really have the luxury of shrugging his shoulders if this class misses. This is the rebuild. These are the assets he chose to turn Michael’s old roster into. You can survive one of them disappointing. Probably two. If this whole group turns into one of those dynasty draft classes we look back on three years later and wonder why everybody talked themselves into it, Richmond is going to be down here for a while.
No pressure or anything, Jon.
Just your entire franchise.
At least there is a plan now. That sounds like an insult to Michael, and it is.

I can look at Richmond and understand what Jon is trying to build. He came into a bad situation, accepted that it was bad instead of spending a year pretending otherwise, got younger and started over. There’s something here if these guys develop. Tyson in particular can change the complexion of this thing pretty quickly once he gets healthy, and Lemon still has plenty of time to make August completely irrelevant.
I just wish Jon could have gotten one nice month first.

Jon was also supposed to come to Pittsburgh for our meetup during the 2025 NFL Draft and couldn’t make it. I can't help be think that this is the fantasy football gods punishing him for it. I dunno, I don't make the rules.
Richmond starts at #11
Darren, maybe give him some space at work.
6: There was a brief period at the end of last season where I thought Brian had finally accepted reality.

Hollywood looked like it might actually take a year. Nothing dramatic. Sell a little, get younger, stop trying to patch every hole with another trade. Maybe this was finally the soft reload we’ve been waiting a few years to see Brian attempt.
Then Brian remembered he doesn’t own his 2027 first.
More importantly, Brian remembered he’s Brian.
Fuck it. We ball. We are competing again.

Honestly, rebuilding without your own first is just volunteering to suck for somebody else. There’s no dignity in that. You go 4-10, spend four months miserable, and then some asshole (me) gets Cam Coleman out of it.
So the brief Hollywood rebuild ended about as quickly as it started.

The official announcement came during that ridiculous three-way trade this offseason when Brian moved a late first and came out of it with Nico Collins. Of course he did. There are certain trades where you see the Sleeper notification and need a minute to figure out what each team is doing.
Brian getting Nico required no such investigation.
Oh. Hollywood is doing this shit again.

Somewhere in Los Angeles, Aaron Donald is looking at the Rams loading up for another Super Bowl run and thinking about coming out of retirement. Brian never even made it that far. Somebody reminded him where his 2027 first was and he was back.
I kind of love it.
Not necessarily the roster. The roster is why he’s ninth.

But Brian has never really been built for the patient dynasty thing where you spend two years collecting picks and talking about your “window.” He wants to have a chance. Sometimes the chance is legitimate. Sometimes the chance requires explaining to the rest of us why Parker Washington is about to become a household name. Doesn't matter. Brian can talk himself into it.

When he first came into the league as Jensen’s co-owner, Hollywood went on a completely insane Cinderella run all the way to the championship game. Then we watched Tanish win the whole thing last season when everyone thought he would be the easy playoff matchup.
So now Brian gets to carry that around in his head forever.
Why not me?
Why not this team?
Why not now?

And there are enough players here that I can’t completely dismiss it. Jordan Love. Egbuka. Parker Washington. Nico now sitting at the top of the receiver room. Then Brian got Jeremiyah Love at 1.01, which gave Hollywood the exact kind of young centerpiece this roster badly needed.
There is a version of this season where this works.
That sentence is going to keep Brian alive for months.
The problem comes about six names further down the roster.
Hollywood is dangerously thin.
Brian is a papercut away from starting Malik Washington or Croskey-Merritt and then spending all week telling us it was actually a matchup decision.

That’s what keeps Hollywood down here at #9. I can see the path. I actually see it pretty clearly. Nico changes the team. Jeremiyah Love could change it even more. Egbuka takes the step, Jordan Love gives him stability at quarterback, maybe one of the thinner pieces hits and suddenly this ranking looks stupid.
Just please nobody get hurt.
Nobody have a bye week either.
Actually if we could get the NFL to stagger Hollywood’s bye weeks specifically, that would help.

Brian doesn’t need this team to be the best roster in the league. He already knows that. Get in. Stay alive. Let somebody else’s superteam have one horrible semifinal Sunday and suddenly we’re all sitting here watching Hollywood do the Cinderella bullshit again.
He’s done it before.
Tanish just reminded everyone it can happen.
And Brian already traded away the incentive to be bad.
There was really only one possible outcome here.
The rebuild lasted about three weeks.
Hollywood is back.
7: There is a built-in disadvantage to hosting the PDL podcast that I don’t think Darren and I fully appreciated when we started doing this seven years ago.
We never shut the fuck up.
We have recorded over 333 hours of podcast content about a 12-team fantasy football league.
That is deranged.

There are television shows that were canceled after eight episodes because America had heard enough. Darren and I have apparently decided the world needed 333 hours of us discussing whether somebody’s fourth running back has standalone value.
And somewhere in those 333 hours, Darren has said something negative about every single one of you.
Probably multiple things.
Now, every August, somebody remembers that Darren said their team sucked on a podcast in 2022, and suddenly it's bulletin-board material.
Meanwhile Joe can silently dismantle an entire franchise, and nobody even knows what his voice sounds like.
There are benefits to being silent.
Darren and I have never discovered them.

He’s been the primary mouthpiece of the podcast forever, so naturally he has become one of the easiest people in the league to root against. Every take is archived. Every bad prediction can be found. Every player he hated eventually gets screenshotted the second he scores 30 points.
And after all of that, the really irritating part is that the Philadelphia Thunder are still sitting here at #2.
Again.
This is where Greg will accuse me of sucking Darren's dick.
Greg, I know.
I can literally hear you saying it while I write this.
Give me like four paragraphs. I’ll try to find something mean.
The problem is the roster is loaded.

Jahmyr Gibbs and Brock Bowers are two of the cleanest superstar assets you can own in this format. Gibbs spent the beginning of August holding in and then ended up signing a deal worth as much as $75.75 million, making him the highest-paid running back in NFL history.
Of course Darren owns him.
Even Darren’s fantasy players negotiate successfully.

Bowers is currently doing Bowers shit in Raiders camp and was making explosive plays against Houston in joint practice today. CeeDee Lamb. Garrett Wilson. Luther Burden. There are stars, young players, veterans, and then you get to the bench and start finding guys who would be in the weekly lineup for half the league.
That’s what separates this team.
It isn’t even really the starting lineup.
It’s the depth underneath it.
Darren doesn’t really have that Sunday morning experience where your starter gets ruled out and you stare at your bench like you’ve never seen these people before.
He just puts another guy in.
Fuck off.
There.
Greg, we're back.
If Darren had spent the last seven years quietly building this roster, everyone would probably look at Philadelphia and just say he's one of the best owners in the league.
Instead we know too much.
We know the prospects he hated.
We know the trades he thought were stupid.
We know exactly how he feels about your quarterback.
We've heard the Jared Goff takes. The Jayden Daniels takes. The entire annual seminar on why everyone else values running backs incorrectly.
Three hundred and thirty-three hours.
There are federal investigations with less recorded testimony.
Yet the standings keep bailing him out.
Philadelphia is on a three-year playoff streak, and this year the voting put Darren only 0.3 points away from the #1 team. His ballots ranged from first to fourth.
Nobody thinks this team is bad.
That's probably the strongest endorsement possible because I know at least half of you would rank Darren 11th out of spite if you could plausibly defend it.
There is also something very fitting about Darren being #2 rather than #1.
Second gives him something to complain about.
First would be too dangerous.

If we actually gave Darren the top spot, the podcast would become unlistenable. We'd get a 19-minute opening monologue about how the league finally understands roster construction followed by three weeks of him pretending the ranking doesn't matter to him.
Nobody needs that.
So #2 is perfect.
He gets the validation.
Mike gets the target.
Greg gets to accuse me of sucking Darren's dick.
And the rest of us get another full season to root against the guy who has spent seven years publicly documenting why all of our teams are built incorrectly.
Everybody wins.
Except probably whoever has to play Philadelphia.
8: I have spent years making fun of Welch for not trading.

You send Welch an offer, and you know that asset is safe. Nothing reckless is happening here. This is a man who has built a reputation for treating every dynasty transaction like it requires environmental review. Welch doesn't get caught up in the moment. Welch doesn't panic. Welch certainly isn't going to wake up one morning and randomly sell a major asset for fifty cents on the dollar.
So anyway, he traded Breece Hall to Greg for two seconds.
Two.
Seconds.
I still don't understand it.
Not a first. Not some young player Welch really liked. Not even one of those disgusting six-piece trades where a bunch of nickels adds up to a dollar.
Breece Hall.
Two second-round picks.
Done.
And this came from Welch. Michael used to do this, and we'd assume he had already changed his mind before the trade processed.
The explanation, apparently, was that Dallas had enough running backs.
Let's check.
Bucky Irving. David Montgomery.
Okay.
Then RJ Harvey, James Conner and Tony Pollard.
Welch looked at that room and decided Breece was clutter.

For about one glorious notification cycle this week, by the way, Welch looked like a fucking prophet. Breece went down untouched at Jets practice, and every fantasy player who got the alert immediately assumed something horrible happened. I can only imagine Welch opening his phone, seeing "non-contact injury" and slowly leaning back in his chair. Wait, didn't he already do this with LaPorta when we clowned him for trading him, and then he got hurt too... wait a second... what's going on here?

What makes the trade so much worse is that Dallas is good. This isn't some team sitting at #11 where you're moving anything that won't be around in three years. Amon-Ra. Trey McBride. Drake London. Fannin. Those are pieces you can absolutely win with. Goff and Kyler aren't exciting enough to make anyone start drawing up championship parade routes, but they're fine. Christian Watson, McLaurin. Fine. There is a lot of "fine" once you get past the top end, but the top end is real.

David Montgomery will probably score 16 touchdowns from the two-yard line and make this entire paragraph useless. Bucky can carry a backfield. Maybe Fannin goes insane. Maybe Christian Watson finally puts together an entire season without making his fantasy owner learn a new part of the human leg.
There are ways Dallas gets there.
But there used to be a much easier way.

What’s frustrating about Dallas is that this isn’t some declining roster hanging around off reputation. Welch has legitimately good players. There’s enough here for a third straight playoff appearance. There’s enough here to make me nervous ranking my own team ahead of him. He doesn’t need five things to break perfectly. He needs a couple.
He also needs Bucky Irving and David Montgomery to remain upright because the safety net gets old pretty fast.
James Conner will turn 63 sometime around Week 8.
Tony Pollard has been in the league long enough that I still mentally associate him with Ezekiel Elliott.
And RJ Harvey is sitting there being asked to justify why Breece Hall was apparently excess inventory.
No pressure, kid.

This is the first team where I really think the playoff line starts getting blurry. Dallas can make it. I wouldn’t be surprised at all. Amon-Ra and McBride alone give Welch weekly advantages that some teams just don't have.
But somebody has to be seventh.
And when sixth and seventh are this close, sometimes the difference comes down to one player.
Like, hypothetically, Breece Hall.
Sorry Welch.
I tried to move on.
#7 Dallas Drip.
9: There was a time when ranking Greg 12th wasn’t even really an opinion.
We’d get to the bottom of the rankings, Greg would be sitting there with some horrific roster he had intentionally created to have the lowest PF, and we would treat him as a floating bye week.
He did this for years.
And now the London Monarchs are 4.
Justin Herbert. Bo Nix. Bijan Robinson. Chris Olave.
And then Greg apparently spent this offseason preparing for Trump tarriffs on RBs.
Bijan.
Breece Hall.
Derrick Henry.
Quinshon Judkins.
He's just hoarding them at this point.
The rest of us lose a running back and immediately start opening depth charts trying to figure out whether some 26-year-old special teamer is secretly next in line for 11 touches.
Greg loses one and has to decide which other starting NFL running back he feels like using.
That’s depth.
And somehow, despite assembling probably the best running back room in the league next to Wichita, Greg will still message you on a Sunday morning sounding like the fucking season is over.
That’s Greg.

Mike is right there with him in the PDL pessimism rankings, but Greg has perfected a very specific form of it where he can have four things go right and immediately locate the fifth thing that didn’t.
Bijan: 26 points.
Breece: 19.
Henry: two touchdowns.
Greg:
“I don’t know man. Judkins only had 11 carries.”
You cannot help him.

Justin Herbert might actually be the perfect quarterback for Greg because this offseason Mike McDaniel has been openly raving about how quickly Herbert is picking up the new offense. McDaniel even watched Herbert throw a training-camp interception and called it a “great rep.”

That Herbert/McDaniel pairing is also a huge part of why London has become genuinely scary. Herbert has had the physical talent forever, and now he gets an offensive coordinator whose entire reason for being there is basically to see how ridiculous they can make this thing. The early camp reports have been glowing.
Olave just got paid too. Four years, up to $132 million, $90 million guaranteed.
At some point Greg is going to run out of things to worry about and I’m genuinely interested to see what happens to him.
He’ll find something.

The funny part is that #4 almost feels low when you remember where this team came from. The league basically agreed on London. Nobody had them outside the playoff group. Greg’s range was third to sixth, which might be the least controversial thing we’ve voted on so far.
That’s how far this has gone.
We aren’t debating whether Greg’s rebuild worked anymore.
It worked.
It’s over.
You don’t get to call yourself rebuilding when Bijan Robinson gets hurt and your emergency plan is Breece Hall.
Sorry.
You’re one of the assholes now.

The only thing keeping London out of the absolute top tier is that there are still a couple spots where the roster isn’t quite as disgusting as the teams above him. Tight end isn't anything special. There are teams with more overwhelming receiver rooms.
Whatever.
I’m nitpicking because we’re at #4.
That’s what happens up here.

Greg spent years collecting tiny pieces of value while the rest of us laughed at the roster, and somehow all those stupid little transactions eventually became Herbert, Bijan, Breece, Olave, Nix, and a million RBs.
It is probably the most successful full teardown we’ve seen in the PDL.
Greg will read that sentence and immediately think I’m trying to jinx him.
Good.
#4 London Monarchs
Congrats Greg.
Your team is great.
I’m sorry.
10: Mike has officially run out of excuses.
Second straight year at #1.
And somehow I think this version of Southern Oregon might be better than the one we ranked first last year.
Josh Allen. De’Von Achane. Ashton Jeanty. Justin Jefferson. Puka Nacua. George Pickens. Rome Odunze. Jaylen Waddle.
Then you get past the starters, and there are still actual players down there. TreVeyon Henderson. Michael Wilson. Courtland Sutton.
It’s obnoxious.
Last year there were at least places where you could squint and convince yourself the league was overrating the Smoke. I don’t really have that this time.
We tried on the podcast.
Darren got to tight end.
That was basically it.

And even that conversation somehow ended with us realizing Mike still has future draft capital and could just go buy a better tight end if he gets bored. At one point Trey McBride came up, and both of us immediately wanted to stop talking about it because nobody needs to give Mike ideas.
So I'm not doing the thing where I spend the next six paragraphs desperately trying to manufacture weaknesses because this is a power ranking and apparently journalistic integrity matters now.
The team is great.
The much bigger concern is the owner.
Mike can tilt.
Oh my God can Mike tilt.
Nobody in the PDL can go from “I have the best team in the league” to investigating a full organizational teardown faster because Justin Jefferson has two catches at halftime.
This is a man who could start Sunday projected to win by 35, watch Achane get stuffed on 3rd-and-1, and begin mentally exploring whether 2028 is a stronger draft class.
Josh Allen just opened Buffalo’s new stadium by going 6-for-8 for 111 yards and a touchdown in his first preseason action.
Achane touched the ball seven times on Miami’s opening drive Friday and finished it with a touchdown.
Seven carries on one preseason drive.

Jeanty is heading into Year 2 working on becoming a more complete passing-down back. Jefferson doesn't have to play with NINE, so that's a huge upgrade. Puka is Puka. Pickens finally had the breakout everyone spent years waiting for. There isn't some hidden offseason disaster we're trying to talk ourselves around.
Tanish just spent an entire offseason poisoning everyone's brain because he proved you can sneak into the playoffs and win the whole thing.
Mike gets the opposite problem.
Nobody is letting him sneak anywhere.
Southern Oregon is the team everyone is going to want to beat. Mike isn't getting the fun underdog story. Nobody is going to call this Cinderella if it works.
If the Smoke win, everyone will shrug and say:
Yeah. Well, that was supposed to happen.
Fair or not, that's where we're at.
The funniest part is that Mike's ranking range went all the way down to fifth.
Whoever did that, I respect the attempt.
I don't understand it.
Maybe you know something.
Maybe Mike submitted a ballot.
That's probably the most believable explanation.

Because if there is one owner capable of looking at Josh Allen, Jefferson, Puka, Achane, Jeanty, Pickens, Waddle and all that depth and deciding there are four better teams, it's Mike approximately eleven minutes after one of them pulls a hamstring.
Mike finished with a 1.7 average, Darren was right behind him at 2.0, and Southern Oregon takes the top spot for the second straight season.
Last year he didn't cash it in.
Fine. Fantasy football happens.
Do it twice, and now it gets funny.
You can only be preseason champion for so long before somebody asks where the actual trophy is.

And this may genuinely be one of the best rosters the PDL has ever had. We threw that question around on the podcast and couldn't dismiss it, especially considering how much stronger the league is from top to bottom this year.
So that's it.
No rebuild to explain. No darkhorse case to make. No future window we're waiting on.
You're here, Mike.
Try not to freak the fuck out.
#1 Southern Oregon Smoke
11: This is where the rebuilds start getting interesting.
Connecticut is basically a brokerage account. Richmond is currently being held together by athletic tape. Dubrovnik actually has players.
A lot of good ones, too.

Jaxson Dart, Omarion Hampton, Tetairoa McMillan, Colston Loveland, Trevor Lawrence. This thing is young as hell, and for the first time in a while you can look at the Dragons roster and see where it’s going. They’re still paper thin. An injury or two in the wrong place and we’re going to be scrolling pretty far down the roster. But the foundation is there.
Which makes the Carnell Tate trade even more fucking confusing.
I know we’ve beaten this to death already. I’m going to continue.
He drafted Tate at 1.04.
Carnell Tate then became the fourth overall pick in the actual NFL Draft.
And Dubrovnik traded him for a late 2027 first.
That’s it.
I’ve gone back to the trade several times thinking I forgot another piece.
Nope.
The explanation, as far as I can tell, is that the Dragons are focused on competing next year.
Carnell Tate is 21.
What were we worried about, his expiring contract?

This is the part of dynasty rebuilding that makes me insane. Somewhere along the way we decided every team needs to announce a competitive window like we’re running an actual NFL front office. You’re allowed to accidentally be good early. Sleeper will not reject your playoff berth because the rebuild was scheduled through Q3 2027.
Especially after what we watched Tanish do.

We are one season removed from that guy winning the entire league when absolutely nobody thought he was going to win the entire league. We should have learned something from this. Get into the playoffs with a pulse and weird shit happens.
Dubrovnik had a chance to be one of those teams.
Honestly, they still might be.

That’s what I like about this roster. Dart is heading into Year 2 and already gives the Dragons something legitimate to watch at quarterback. Hampton and Tet are exactly the type of young cornerstone assets you want while coming out of a rebuild. Loveland had 58 catches for 713 yards as a rookie and almost everyone is already crowning him as the next big thing at TE.
There’s enough here.
Not enough depth. Definitely not enough depth. But enough actual talent that I don’t really understand the insistence that this year doesn’t count.
Roger Goodell is currently promising us an NFL franchise in another country without even knowing when that’s happening. Dubrovnik has somehow developed a more rigid timeline:
Next year.
Next year we compete.
This year we develop.
Please disregard the 21-year-old receiver we just traded because apparently he was getting in the way.
I am beating this dead horse tongue-in-cheek because I have to face the reality that the Dragons will most likely surpass my own team by next season.

If Dart takes another step, Hampton hits, Tet keeps becoming what everyone thinks he is and Loveland moves into that upper group of dynasty tight ends, this team is going to start winning games whether the Brett has authorized it or not.
And then we’re going to talk about the Tate trade again.
A lot.
Because with Tate still sitting on this roster, I’d already be talking myself into Dubrovnik as the annoying darkhorse team nobody really wants to deal with late in the year.
Instead he turned the 1.03 into a future late first and told us to check back next season.
Fine.
But if this team is sitting around .500 in October, I reserve the right to become absolutely unbearable about it.
I am being harsh because Brett is my boy and I know he can handle it; by next year, don't be surprised if this team skyrockets.
12: Tanish has done irreparable damage to this league.
I’m serious.

Before last season, there was at least some shame involved in having the seventh-best team and convincing yourself you could win the championship. You kept that shit to yourself. Maybe you quietly hoped for some matchup luck, but you didn't walk around telling everyone that all you needed was a ticket to the dance.
Then Tanish actually did it.
Now look at us.

Brian thinks Hollywood can make a run. Brett is one Carnell Tate away from apparently becoming the 2007 Giants. I’m sitting here at #6 staring at the decaying remains of the Delco Dreamers thinking, well... if we get in.
Everybody thinks they can win now.
Tanish turned the PDL into a casino full of people who have all personally met the guy who hit the jackpot.
And the worst part is the logic isn't even wrong.
He proved it.

Boulder got into the playoffs last year, caught fire at exactly the right time and won the whole fucking thing while starting players in the championship game that we were trying to remember on the pod. Samaje Perine was involved. Mack Hollins was involved. Nobody should win a dynasty championship like that.
Tanish did.
So congratulations on the championship, but also fuck you for what you've done to everyone else's decision-making.
Now he enters this season at #5 with a team that is somehow one of the strangest defending champions I can remember.
Start with quarterback.
Drake Maye.
Caleb Williams.
Jayden Daniels.
Tanish has spent what feels like the entire offseason trying to trade one of these guys without actually trading one of these guys.
You could ask Tanish if he watched the Eagles game and 15 minutes later he's explaining why you should give him two starters and a first for Caleb Williams.
We know they're available, Tanish.
Everyone knows.
At this point, those three have been on the market longer than some houses.

And I understand why he hasn't just dumped one. They're insanely valuable dynasty assets. Maye just finished second in NFL MVP voting and took New England to the Super Bowl. Caleb has another year in Ben Johnson's offense. Jayden is not having the best off-season for his reputation, but still a highly valuable SF dynasty asset. This isn't some QB room where you have to convince people Tanner McKee secretly has top-12 upside.
But eventually the theoretical value has to become something you can actually start.

That was probably the biggest thing Darren and I kept coming back to. Boulder has a ton of dynasty value trapped at one position. Move one quarterback and suddenly the depth problem starts looking a lot less annoying.
Maybe Jayden will force the issue.

He's currently in an actual dispute with LSU because they gave his old No. 5 to another player, to the point that his representatives sent the school a cease-and-desist over the use of his name, image and likeness.
Boulder Bears: #5.
At least one person on this roster is fucking furious about it.
The rest of the team is still good enough that I understand why Tanish has been reluctant to mess with it too much.

JSN is a monster. Malik Nabers comes back. Jonathan Taylor was basically the engine that made last year's run possible. Rashee Rice. There are enough high-end names here that when everything is healthy, Boulder looks much scarier than your typical fifth-ranked team.
Then you hit the bench and remember how Tanish ended up starting Samaje Perine in a championship game.
There it is.
The depth is still shaky.

Kincaid goes down and tight end gets ugly fast. The running backs behind Taylor are more useful than terrifying. Travis Hunter remains this bizarre fantasy science experiment where everyone is still trying to figure out how much actual receiver we're getting. Nabers is returning from injury.
And yet Tanish seems completely unbothered by all of this.
Why wouldn't he be?
He already won with worse.

Boulder does still own its 2027 first, which is important because half this league has already pawned theirs off somewhere. Tanish isn't trapped. If the Bears start well and he finally moves one of those quarterbacks, this roster can get materially better pretty quickly.
There are teams above Boulder that I trust more week to week. Deeper lineups. Fewer places where one injury makes the roster start looking familiar in a bad way.
But I am done telling Tanish what a championship roster is supposed to look like.
We tried that.
He put Samaje Perine in the lineup and hung a banner.
Nobody will ever rebuild responsibly again.
